audit.whatIsWrong: Two stages had prose that contradicted their own chart entry: Level 1 is marked Graves but the why said Galio 'wins most level-1 exchanges', and Level 6 is marked Graves but both layers said Hero's Entrance makes it Galio's spike.
audit.why: Level 1 belongs to Graves because his shotgun out-ranges Galio's only ability. Level 6 belongs to Graves because Collateral Damage is a 100s nuke that front-loads onto the first champion it hits — Galio's R is a map tool, not a duel answer. Neither layer had ever mentioned Collateral Damage, which is exactly why the level-6 row looked wrong.
audit.corrected: Level-1 and Level-6 whys now state the Graves reason and give Galio's actual play (farm behind minions; leave the duel and R elsewhere), so text and chart agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: Graves's ultimate was absent from every field in both layers, so the level-6 power spike had no stated cause.
audit.why: Collateral Damage is 100/80/60s, 1000 range, deals heavy damage to the first champion it hits and only then cones out. That is the level-6 swing and it was never written down.
audit.corrected: Collateral Damage named in the level-6 spike, whys[4], full phases[4].why and the foe-wants list, with its 100s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page said Smoke Screen 'blinds you and your empowered passive auto'. It does not blind. It also never mentioned that Graves's autos are stopped by minions.
audit.why: Riot's own text for Smoke Screen: it 'creates a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range' plus initial magic damage and a brief slow — a nearsight, no miss chance, so Colossal Smash still lands. And New Destiny: 'Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units.' Standing with a minion between you and Graves removes most of his lane damage, which is the single biggest interaction in this matchup and it was missing.
audit.corrected: Blind claim removed and replaced with sight-cut plus slow; minion-block written into the level 1-2 spike, wants.you, early, whys and the Key Ability Interactions block.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Track Quickdraw' with no number anywhere, and Smoke Screen's cooldown never appeared.
audit.why: Quickdraw is 16/15/14/13/12 but Riot's text says basic attacks lower it, so it is only a punish window while he is not hitting you. Smoke Screen is 26s at rank 1 — the longest cooldown in his lane kit and the safest moment to step up.
audit.corrected: 16s Quickdraw (with the attack-refund caveat) and 26s Smoke Screen now carried in the cooldown block, do's line, trading rules and Key Ability Interactions.

audit.why: Plated Steelcaps / Sorcerer's Shoes split is already right for a pure-AD lane and the armour side is already called out in the TL;DR.

audit.whatIsWrong: The loading tip closed with 'Anti-heal if he sustains'.
audit.why: Graves has no heal or sustain anywhere in his kit — no heal flag on any ability. That line is dead space on the loading screen.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the minion-block rule, which is the thing a Galio actually gets wrong in this lane.

edits.after: Graves owns the opening — his shotgun out-ranges your single ability and Shield of Durand is weakest against pure AD. Pellets cannot pass through units, so last-hit behind a minion.

edits.before: Respect Graves at level 1 — you have one ability and no engage, and his shotgun pellet autos plus Quickdraw burst chunk you before you can answer. His damage is pure AD, so Shield of Durand's reduction is at its weakest here (the channel only shines against magic), and the taunt is what makes W worth pressing, not the mitigation — don't channel expecting to sponge his trades. Last-hit at the tip of Q's center column and wait. At level 3, once Q-tornado, W-taunt and E-knockup are all up, you have a window: bait his Quickdraw (E) in to trade, then W-taunt locks him and E knocks him up before he can dash back out and re-stack his pellets.
edits.after: Respect Graves at level 1 — you have one ability and no engage, and his shotgun plus Quickdraw burst chunk you before you can answer. His damage is pure AD, so Shield of Durand's reduction is at its weakest here (the channel only shines against magic), and the taunt is what makes W worth pressing, not the mitigation. Your real defence is the wave: his four pellets cannot pass through units, so last-hit with a minion in the way and he loses most of his damage. At level 3, once Winds of War, the taunt and Justice Punch are all up, bait his Quickdraw in, taunt him, and knock him up — 16s at rank 1, and only his attacks landing on you shorten it.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a farm-and-bait phase — you only out-trade him if he greeds a Quickdraw dash into your taunt range, so invite that, then W-taunt into E-knockup into Q-tornado for a full combo. Don't chase him through Smoke Screen; his W blinds you and your empowered passive auto, and he kites your fixed E distance the moment your dash is on cooldown. Six is where you stop trying to win the duel — Hero's Entrance lets you flag onto a sidelane or a fight and swing the map, which is your actual win condition here. Shove the wave and roam with R rather than feeding him free pellet trades at home.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a farm-and-bait phase — you only out-trade him if he greeds a Quickdraw dash into taunt range, so invite that, then taunt into Justice Punch into Winds of War for a full combo. Smoke Screen does not blind you: it cuts your sight and slows, so Colossal Smash still lands, but do not chase him through it, and note the cloud is a 26s cooldown you can step up on. Six is where you stop trying to win the duel — Collateral Damage out-bursts you and Hero's Entrance lets you swing another lane instead. Shove the wave and roam with R.

edits.before: This is Graves's game if it goes long. A tanky-ADC Graves (Eclipse or Collector into bruiser items) kites outside your fixed E range and shreds you with pellet autos while your damage and durability flatten. Your value is no longer the duel — it's R-presence and W-taunt peel for your carries in 5v5s. Force your team to fight around your engage; never splitpush into him, because he wins the isolated 1v1 and your global is wasted just standing next to him.
edits.after: This is Graves's game if it goes long. A tanky-ADC Graves (Eclipse or Collector into bruiser items) kites outside your 650 Justice Punch and shreds you with pellets while your damage and durability flatten, and Collateral Damage still opens on you first. Your value is no longer the duel — it's R-presence and taunt peel for your carries in 5v5s. Force your team to fight around your engage; never splitpush into him, because he wins the isolated 1v1 and your global is wasted standing next to him.

notes: Corrected a hard factual error: the page said Graves's Smoke Screen blinds Galio and his empowered passive auto. Riot's current text has no blind — it is a sight-range cut plus initial magic damage and a brief slow, so Colossal Smash still connects. Also added the minion-block rule from New Destiny ('Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units'), which was absent everywhere and is the most valuable line in the matchup. Graves's ultimate, Collateral Damage, was never named in either layer; adding it is what makes the Level 6 = Graves chart row read correctly instead of looking like a data error. I did NOT claim Quickdraw reloads his shotgun — an older line implied it and Riot's current text only says basic attacks lower its cooldown, so I dropped rather than restated it. Win rate checks out: packet and MC_WR_TABLES/MC_REAL_GAMES agree at 46.72% over 122 games.
